clue.text: See 25
Old woman upset over exam lacking principles

indicators.note: in a down clue, something upset is turned upside down, so its letters read bottom to top

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old woman
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is upset about an exam testing ethics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' is slang for one's mother; in a down clue 'over' places the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone amoral has no moral standards at all, neither good nor bad values guiding conduct.

clue.text: Way horse eats good with bad meat in this dish

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a mixed coat
G is the abbreviation for good
food gone bad has gone off

explanation.surface: A dish in which a horse feeds on good food and on spoiled meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The good letter sits inside the horse, after the way and before the bad. The definition reads as a whole: the dish in which meat appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroganoff is a Russian dish of strips of beef cooked in a sour cream sauce.

clue.text: Pound fare for travellers here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to strike repeatedly, as wind or waves do
second meaning: a station or train counter selling food

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money and 'fare' like a ticket price; the verb sense is battering, and fare here is food.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to batter; a station or railway buffet is the refreshment counter where passengers buy snacks.

clue.text: Court risk associated with railway

parts.note: to take a chance is to take a risk
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone courts danger by getting involved with the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' reads as a verb, to court risk, but it is the noun defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court, historically the Lord Chancellor's court of equity.

clue.text: Mercian king to hold out for hearing

indicators.note: something offered for hearing is meant to be listened to, so the sound counts, not the spelling

parts.note: to hold something out is to offer it

explanation.surface: An ancient king refuses to give way while awaiting his trial.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the verb meaning to proffer is pronounced just like the king's name. Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled Mercia in the eighth century and is remembered for the earthwork Offa's Dyke.

clue.text: Simply lock for solid support

parts.note: 'but' can mean only or simply, as in 'but a child'
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Merely fitting a lock is enough to secure something firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door fastening, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a projecting masonry structure that props up a wall; figuratively any firm prop.

clue.text: Flower pot almost useless

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a crock is an earthenware pot
U/S is the abbreviation for unserviceable, meaning useless

explanation.surface: A flowerpot that is more or less useless.
explanation.walkthrough: U/S (unserviceable) is British military and engineering shorthand for something broken or useless.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small spring bulb plant with cup-shaped purple, white or yellow blooms.

clue.text: Who, ditching wife, dated girl — one's ashamed to hear it

indicators.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for wife, the letter removed
to date someone is to go out with or meet them
Ruth is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man who left his wife to go out with a girl, and should be embarrassed to be told so.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a remark that makes the hearer ashamed.
explanation.definitionFit: A home truth is an unwelcome but accurate fact about oneself, usually painful to be told.

clue.text: Mineral with yellow colour taken after sickness

indicators.note: taken after places one piece behind the other in the answer

parts.note: flu is a common sickness
or is the heraldic tincture gold or yellow

explanation.surface: A yellowish mineral taken as medicine after an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Or is the heraldry word for gold, a frequent crossword source for those two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluor is an older name for fluorite, the calcium fluoride crystal also called fluorspar.

clue.text: Not totally great beginning to Olympic movement

indicators.note: not totally means short of complete, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: large is a synonym for great

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of Olympic

explanation.surface: The Olympic movement has not quite got off to a great start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympic movement' suggests the sporting organisation, but movement is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A largo is a slow, broad section of a symphony or sonata, named from the tempo marking.

clue.text: See 25
Brave man to vex six-footer

parts.note: to gall is to irritate or vex
an ant, as an insect, has six legs

explanation.surface: A courageous fellow sets out to annoy a very tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Six-footer' suggests a tall person; any insect has six feet, and the ant is the usual one.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun a gallant is a dashing, courageous gentleman, often attentive to women.

clue.text: Siren never has time for leading lady

indicators.note: if something never has a thing, every instance of it must be taken away

parts.note: a siren is a seductive woman
T is the abbreviation for time; both of these letters go

explanation.surface: A seductive actress is always too busy to play the main role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Never has' means the word loses every T it contains, here two of them, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female ruler of an empire, a lady who leads a whole realm.

clue.text: Edited parchment, most faded: wicked things therein

indicators.note: therein means inside that, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the most faded colour is the palest
imps are small mischievous demons

explanation.surface: An old manuscript, much faded and revised, hides wicked secrets in its text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edited' might suggest rearranging letters, but it belongs to the definition: a reused, rewritten parchment.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript whose original writing was scraped off so it could be written over again.

clue.text: Not on bill: two rounds

parts.note: a tab is a bill at a bar or restaurant
each round, circular letter O counts once

explanation.surface: Two rounds of drinks were left off the bar bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on bill' reads as a missing charge, but 'Not on' is the definition: British slang for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is forbidden by custom; 'not on' is the colloquial British phrase for unacceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Repeatedly counter one cold and brutal

parts.note: a bar is a counter in a pub; repeatedly means twice
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone keeps countering a cold, brutal opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a verb meaning to oppose, but it is the noun: a pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbaric describes savage cruelty, behaviour felt to be uncivilised and harsh.

clue.text: Keep working steadily in place with yard

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: Toiling steadily at one spot in a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: PL appears in addresses for Place, as in Carlton Pl.
explanation.definitionFit: To ply a trade or tool is to work at it diligently and continuously.

clue.text: Design surrounding emblem is oddly vulgar

indicators.note: to surround something is to sit all around it

parts.note: a plan is a design

indicators.note: oddly points to letters in the odd-numbered positions

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A design around a crest is strangely tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters run across two words, so 'is' contributes its first letter too.
explanation.definitionFit: Plebeian originally meant of the Roman common people and now suggests coarse or unrefined taste.

clue.text: The Spanish sovereign defeated contender

parts.note: los is the Spanish plural word for 'the'
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The King of Spain beat his challenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defeated' reads as a verb with the sovereign as subject, but it modifies contender in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A loser is the person beaten in a match or contest, the one who did not win.

clue.text: Complex read to include feature in Mao's domain

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside
something complex is intricate and tangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the chin is a facial feature

explanation.surface: A complicated text about a feature of Mao's rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' means part of a face, not an article.
explanation.definitionFit: Red China was the Cold War Western name for the communist People's Republic led by Mao Zedong.

clue.text: Tactless remark about Irish beast

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Someone makes an insensitive comment about an Irish animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beast' sounds like an insult tied to the remark but is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe is an African animal, the tallest living land mammal with a very long neck.

clue.text: Rock enjoyable on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio things are heard, not seen, so sound matters over spelling

parts.note: nice means pleasant or enjoyable

explanation.surface: Rock music that is pleasant to hear on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music, but it is stone; the G is silent, so the word is pronounced like 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gneiss is a coarse-grained metamorphic stone with banded layers of minerals.

clue.text: Ring for captain to supply troop with weapons?

parts.note: to supply a group with weapons, as the clue's closing words add, is to arm it
a band is a group or troop

explanation.surface: A call to the captain to equip his unit with arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a phone call; it is a band of cloth round the arm. Clue order puts troop first, answer order the arming.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports team captain wears an armband, a loop of fabric worn round the upper sleeve.

clue.text: Gold cask for beer contains malt initially for season

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: a container holds something inside it

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for beer or wine

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of malt

explanation.surface: A golden beer barrel holds malt for the brewing season.
explanation.walkthrough: AU comes from the Latin aurum.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is the season between summer and winter, known in America as fall.

clue.text: Fuss about an American soldier showing slow movement

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece encloses the rest

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother
the indefinite article as a single letter
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A fuss over a US soldier who is moving sluggishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow movement' sounds like the soldier dawdling, but it is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a section of a symphony or concerto played at a leisurely tempo.

clue.text: Beat back workers in sober performance

indicators.note: going back means reading from right to left

parts.note: to cane is to beat with a stick

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, sober
men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Fending off staff during a teetotal show.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is short for teetotal, a standard crossword way to say sober.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactment is the acting out of a role or scene, so a staging or rendition of it.

clue.text: Dance tour great that draws in underweight people?

parts.note: a tour or journey
people who weigh little can be described collectively as the definite article plus the opposite of heavy
great in the sense of wonderful

explanation.surface: A great dance tour that tempts slim people to join in.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase TRIP THE LIGHT FANTASTIC comes from Milton; the clue reads it as a tour plus something great that pulls in light people, the question mark flagging the whimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an old, jocular way of saying to go out dancing, especially lightly and nimbly.

clue.text: Axe discovered in extremely spiritual wood

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the two end letters of spiritual
ash is a hardwood tree and its timber

explanation.surface: An axe found in a sacred forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like the tool, but it is the verb meaning to cut drastically.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a budget or jobs is to cut them sharply, which is also to slash them.

clue.text: Genre making comeback in some terrific stories

indicators.note: a comeback returns the way it went, so the letters read backwards
some of a phrase means a run of letters inside it

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A literary category is enjoying a revival in some great tales.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the end of terrific and the start of stories, then reads right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a category of fiction, film and art built on imagined science and technology.

clue.text: Confession being task of Christian era?

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, dates the Christian era
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: Confessing sins was a duty in Christian times.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in reverse of clue order: the era comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is an acknowledgement that something, usually discreditable, is true.
